source.title: Not-Just-Scaling Laws: Towards a Better Understanding of the Downstream Impact of Language Model Design Decisions
source.authors: Emmy Liu; Amanda Bertsch; Lintang Sutawika; Lindia Tjuatja; Patrick Fernandes; Lara Marinov; Michael Chen; Shrey Singhal; Carolin Lawrence; Aditi Raghunathan; Kiril Gashteovski; Graham Neubig

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method and outcome from pretraining-loss scaling laws: it evaluates how well scale-based and richer feature-based predictors predict downstream benchmark scores, and fits power laws to benchmark performance.
record.gate_note: The paper fits Kaplan-style power laws to downstream task scores and reports task-specific fit quality, and compares cross-validated downstream-score prediction using scale features with prediction using all features. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss across parameter, token, or compute scales, test extrapolation to much larger runs, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Confirmatory data-mixture losses and architectural feature analyses concern design choices, not the scaling-law outcomes named by the other versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits Kaplan-style power laws of downstream benchmark scores against parameters and tokens for 92 open base models. It also cross-validates a scale-only predictor of downstream scores. Both results bear on V6, downstream predictability from scale, within the observed range (interpolation only). No result concerns pretraining loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or loss-based fit-dependence.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Adding architecture, data-composition and free-generation features to N and D improves downstream-score prediction by 3–28% relative on all 12 benchmarks. Task-specific power-law fits vary widely in quality, R2 0.29–0.85, with U-shaped TruthfulQA. Non-scale architecture choices have minor effects compared with data composition and scale. Predictions are interpolative within the observed range.
record.recipe_differences: This is an observational meta-analysis of open pretrained models with tree-based cross-validated downstream-score predictors and task-specific power-law fits. It does not reproduce the original held-out language-modeling-loss measurement or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark/task changes the fitted power-law R2 and prediction error; the authors describe task-specific scaling trends and note TruthfulQA's U-shaped pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-scale architectural choices (positional embedding, LayerNorm, attention variant) have small, bias-corrected effects on downstream accuracy, e.g. RoPE +1.5pp and RMSNorm +2.3pp, compared with scale and data composition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At matched scale, architecture details shift downstream benchmark accuracy only slightly (a downstream analogue of V4).

fits_no_version.finding: Data composition (code share, web share) predicts downstream scores beyond N and D; confirmatory 460M runs partly replicate this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining data mix shifts downstream scaling curves at fixed N and D.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The scaling analysis is observational and concerns downstream task scores rather than held-out pretraining loss. The authors state the model sample is limited, especially above 50B parameters, unevenly distributed across sizes and data distributions, and subject to selection and time effects. Tree-based predictors prioritize interpolation within the observed range (10M-100B parameters, 50B-3T tokens) rather than extrapolation. Some evaluations omit models because of loading or evaluation-harness errors.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Confirmatory data-mixture loss values (Tables 10–11) and architectural-effect estimates (Table 12) were not included because they do not measure the scaling-law outcomes named by the tested versions.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss vs N, D or C is not measured.
No extrapolation: the tree predictors interpolate within 10M–100B parameters and 50B–3T tokens.
No loss comparison at fixed parameter count. Architecture effects are measured only on downstream accuracy, observationally.
Only text-pretrained base models are studied.
Untested: prediction from pretraining loss, and extrapolation of downstream scores to larger scales.
No test of how exponents or the allocation depend on parameter counting, schedule, data or fitting method for loss laws.

missing.what: Log-linear (parametric) scale-only baseline MAE per task. It is much worse than the tree scale-only predictor on several tasks (GSM8k 11.03 vs 6.04; MMLU 0-shot 9.12 vs 4.76) and near the median baseline on TruthfulQA (3.40 vs 3.72). This bears on how predictable downstream scores are from a simple scaling form.
Per-task number of models evaluated (82 for ANLI, XNLI, LogiQA2, MathQA).

record.verdict_notes: The record's MathQA and LogiQA2 scale-only values were taken from the wrong Table 2 columns; they are corrected above. The R2 rows were moved from V7 to V6, because they measure downstream score vs scale rather than fitting-choice dependence of loss laws. All-features rows were delinked as the study's own method. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, training tokens, or compute.
The authors explicitly describe their tree-based predictor as prioritizing interpolation rather than extrapolation; they do not test small-run power-law fits against much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is tested.
Architecture features are examined observationally for downstream task prediction, not by controlled comparisons of pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
The study is limited to text pretraining and does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.

It tests prediction of downstream benchmark scores from parameter count and training tokens, not predictability from held-out pretraining loss or downstream performance at much larger extrapolated scales.

It reports task-specific power-law fit quality and a U-shaped task trend, but does not test how fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation change with parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, fitting methods, or compute.

relationships.condition: Arc, GSM8k, HellaSwag, Winogrande, MMLU 0/5-shot, MathQA (within observed scale range, interpolation)
relationships.reason: Power-law fits of score on N and D give R2 0.70–0.85. The scale-only predictor cuts MAE to roughly a third of the median baseline, e.g. Arc 4.36 vs 13.23.
relationships.display_finding: Power-law fits achieved R² of 0.70–0.85 and reduced MAE to roughly one-third of the median baseline, including Arc's 4.36 versus 13.23.

relationships.condition: HumanEval, Lambada, TruthfulQA, XNLI, ANLI, LogiQA2
relationships.reason: R2 is only 0.29–0.61 and TruthfulQA is U-shaped. Scale-only MAE gains are small for TruthfulQA (2.75 vs 3.72), HumanEval (8.08 vs 11.79) and XNLI (5.11 vs 7.22).
relationships.display_finding: Scale-only fits had R² values of 0.29–0.61 and U-shaped TruthfulQA performance, with MAE comparisons of 2.75 versus 3.72 for TruthfulQA, 8.08 versus 11.79 for HumanEval, and 5.11 versus 7.22 for XNLI.

relationships.reason: Table 2 (text): adding data and architecture features lowers the scale-only MAE by 3–28%, significant on every task, so scale leaves substantial predictable variance unexplained. Rows: the scale-only predictor rows.
relationships.display_finding: Adding data and architecture features reduced scale-only MAE by 3–28%, significantly improving predictions across all 13 benchmark settings.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Scale-feature predictors across the tested downstream benchmarks and settings
reader_labels.reason: Scale-feature predictors achieve lower MAE than the median baseline in all reported cases, supporting downstream score predictability from scale; see the scale-predictor rows.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: All tested downstream benchmarks and settings
reader_labels.reason: The all-features predictor has lower MAE than the scale-only predictor on every reported task, so scale alone is not the best predictor in these comparisons.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TruthfulQA downstream score versus parameters and training tokens
reader_labels.reason: TruthfulQA has the lowest reported fit (R2 0.29), and the authors describe its scaling as U-shaped, showing departure from a single power-law trend.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Fit quality varies substantially by task, but several tasks have relatively high power-law fit values (R2 0.70–0.85), so departures are not uniform across the evaluated benchmarks.
